data.content_ref: inline:The target claims the 1/9 compile.py loss occurred because the guard was 'keyed to the registry's declared data, so mutations that added behaviour outside the registry were not constrained.' This is empirically backwards: compile.py is a build tool, not a data validator. Its 'registry' is the build graph; the 1/9 loss is explained by build-graph coverage (mutations outside the build graph are not exercised), not by a collapse between test and subject. By conflating registry data-model collapse with ordinary coverage failure, the mechanism confuses description (the test exercises a subset) with constraint (the test forces the subject's behavior).
